unverified: This receipt's own content is not covered by command[2]; it did not exist when that scan ran. It is scanned by the pre-commit hook when committed, and by G-3 in CI against the base ref.

`pre-commit install -f`, which opts out of the legacy chaining, was not exercised. The default chaining path was: both hooks were installed and all three commits on this branch ran through them. The -f behaviour is stated in the config header from pre-commit's own documented flag, not from an observed run here.

The G-3 hits in ci/tests/test_gates.py were NOT fixed. That file matches `**/*.py` with no later override, so it is owned by bot-01-systems-backend and out of QUALITY's write scope. The correct fix is a per-line `# pragma: allowlist secret` with a reason, by its owner. No exclude: entry was added here, because excluding the path would also hide a real credential added to it later.
No CI run observed. .github/workflows/ does not exist in this repository; ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml is a template to be copied, and copying it is INFRA's call, not QUALITY's.
The openapi.yaml stub defines no endpoint, so no client was generated from it and no consumer acknowledged it. acknowledgements is [] on purpose rather than pre-filled — see the change document.

CI selects a change document with `ls -1 contracts/changes/*.yaml | head -n1`, which picks the alphabetically first file rather than the one this PR proposes. With one active document that resolves correctly; contracts/changes/README.md documents the archive/ convention that keeps it correct. The workflow itself was not changed — Actions are out of scope for this change.
Did not merge, did not undraft, and did not push to main.

The .pre-commit-config.yaml header was corrected after this observation. An earlier draft claimed installing the framework hook REPLACES the native one; it does not, and the commands above record what actually happens.

This receipt was committed with `git add -f`. .gitignore line 5 ignores .receipts/**/*.json, yet all 22 existing receipts are tracked and both G-2 and the CI template require a committed receipt — so -f is how the existing ones got in, not a workaround invented here. Not fixed in this change: it is a one-line .gitignore question affecting every seat, and .gitignore matches no pattern in ownership.yaml, so G-1 reports it UNOWNED and any edit to it needs a manifest rule first.

A narrower case of the P1 class survives: if a later change happens to touch a path the stale document also declares, coverage is satisfied and the stale document validates it. The complete fix is to require the change document to appear in the diff, which every existing G-4 test would fail — they all write the document to a tmp_path outside the file list — and ci/tests/test_gates.py is owned by bot-01-systems-backend. Needs that owner to update the fixtures alongside the gate.

No regression test was added for the new surface-coverage rule, for the same ownership reason: the gate self-test suite lives in bot-01's path. The behaviour is evidenced by the before/after pair above rather than by a committed test, which is weaker — a future edit to check_contracts.py could silently undo it.

The root cause Greptile named, `ls -1 contracts/changes/*.yaml | head -n1` in ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml, is NOT fixed. That file matches no pattern in ownership.yaml (verified UNOWNED), Actions are out of scope for this change, and the workflow is a template not installed as CI. The gate-level and hook-level guards make the mis-selection fail rather than pass; the selector itself is INFRA's to fix.
